author: Van Tate
title: UNM defensive lineman Jalen McIver gets reps and gets a sack - NewsBreak
text:
By Van Tate No media credit provided. ,
57 minutes ago
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – Jalen McIver made the most of an opportunity in a UNM loss at Boise State last week. The Lobo sophomore defensive lineman was finally pressed into action. Not only did the six foot four 281, 281-pound McIver get playing time, but he also made a contribution.
A few plays after stepping on the field, McIver found himself in the Broncos’ backfield delivering a sack. “I ain’t going to lie to you, when I got the sack, I was, like, shocked at myself, like, when I sacked him, I didn’t realize I sacked him. The whistle blew. I was like, dang, I just got a sack on my first few plays of the game. It was really shocking for real. I was in shock,” said McIver. His stat line for the night read two tackles, a sack, and a tackle for loss. “I do feel like feel like it boosted my confidence a little bit, for real, for real,” said McIver. “Because at first I was down. I wasn’t getting no reps at all, for real, for real. In this game, they gave me a lot of reps, and so, you know, I had to capitalize off of it. I capitalized off of it, made the best of it.”
McIver came to New Mexico from Jones Community College. He played high school football at Hillcrest in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. It’s a place where football is king. McIver said he never entertained the thought of playing college ball for the Crimson Tide. While he lives in Alabama, McIver said he was born in Georgia. He said he was a Georgia Bulldogs fan growing up.
He has always been in an area where football is heavily supported until now. New Mexico is working on building support and McIver is noticing a change. “Like, when I got here, I thought football was big too, since they ain’t got no pro team,” said McIver. “But, then finding out that not a lot of people cared. But, since we got Coach Eck, he changed the program a little bit. I’m starting to see, like, when I go to class, things like that, people ask me how the team is going to do, and who are we going to play next week, and things like that. I’m starting to see people, like, wear our merch around. I think we’re doing good right now.”
UNM is going into homecoming week. They will play the Nevada Wolfpack on Oct. 18. The game has a 7:45 pm start time on FS1.
